nora: Hi team — quick awkward one: my partner Pavel also works at Redwood (EU payroll) and we want to split parental leave between us after our baby arrives mid-August. I'm US payroll, he's EU. How do we request split weeks, handle cross-border pay/top-up, and make sure benefits + taxes are correct?

pavel: Adding detail: we'll each take alternating blocks (4w me, 4w Nora, then 4w shared flex). Need to know if company-paid weeks can be allocated across countries and what forms we both must submit.

jeff: Congrats! Short answer: yes, you can split company-paid parental weeks between two Redwood employees. Both of you must file parental leave requests in your respective portals and indicate "shared leave" and the other employee's name. People Ops will coordinate payroll/top-up locally.

mina: Important practicals: 1) Nora (US): submit parental request + STD claim and FMLA if eligible. 2) Pavel (EU): submit local parental leave request and the EU country-specific benefit claim (e.g., parental allowance) so payroll can calculate top-up. 3) Both upload proof of relationship/intent (birth certificate later) and indicate split schedule.

nora: What about taxes and cross-border withholding? If Pavel is paid in EUR while covering some weeks of US-based work, do we run into double-tax or withholding issues?

jeff: Payroll note: each employee is paid in their home payroll and taxed locally. Company top-up is applied through the local payroll and follows local tax treatment. We don't move pay between countries. If you both are Redwood employees, we coordinate the weeks but each payroll processes its share of the company-paid weeks and any supplement. There shouldn't be cross-border pay shifts, but declare the shared schedule in both portals so records align.

pavel: And benefits for the child — add to the benefits plan within 30 days of birth in each country? That seems messy if the family is split across borders.

mina: Add the child to each employee's benefits where eligible. For global families we usually enroll the child under the parent who is on that country's payroll. If needed, submit dependent documentation to both benefits portals. People Ops can help reconcile a one-time stipend if duplicate coverage causes extra cost.

nora: How does equity vesting and 401k/pension contributions work during alternating paid weeks?

jeff: Company-paid weeks count as payroll for vesting and retirement contributions in each employee's jurisdiction. If either of you take unpaid time, that may pause contributions/deferrals. Submit LOA requests if you plan unpaid stretches so comp can confirm vesting treatment.

hr-bot: AUTOMATED: "Parental leave requests noted for nora and pavel (thread 1762009999). Please upload expected due date confirmation, STD/local benefit claim numbers, and dependent enrollment documents after birth"

pavel: Ops coverage: we'll need a 3-day overlap for handoff and a contractor for infra work during my weeks. Who do I ask for vendor bench?

mina: Open a contractor req with hiring-ops and mark it "parental cover" for expedited vendor bench routing. Include dates, skills, hourly band, and 3-day overlap. Vendor bench turnaround is typically 7-10 business days.

nora: Thanks — uploaded initial leave requests and a draft split schedule. Appreciate the quick answers!

jeff: We'll coordinate offline to confirm payroll cutoffs and exact amounts. Congrats both :heart:
